Summary Description: Dr. Michael Jablonski’s research sits at the intersection of Lie theory and differential geometry, with a focus on the symmetry properties of solvable and semisimple Lie groups and their homogeneous spaces. His work establishes maximal and infinitesimal maximal symmetry results for unimodular solvable groups, develops robust equivalence-class frameworks that transfer symmetry and soliton properties across related groups, and demonstrates that Einstein solvmanifolds and Ricci solitons exhibit maximal symmetry in precise senses. He further provides constructive embedding results, showing how Einstein solvmanifolds can be realized as submanifolds of symmetric spaces via explicit representations, and he advances the reconstruction of real semisimple Lie algebras from Iwasawa subalgebras. Collectively, these contributions deepen the understanding of how algebraic structure governs geometric symmetry in homogeneous spaces and elucidate the rigid, canonical forms such structures must take under various curvature and symmetry constraints. His work often blends deep Lie-theoretic constructions (Iwasawa theory, Satake diagrams, nilradical analysis) with geometric analytic tools (Einstein metrics, Ricci solitons, solvsolitons) to produce unified, canonical pictures of symmetry in noncompact settings.

Core Contributions: Shows unimodular solvable Lie groups admit left-invariant metrics with maximal symmetry (largest possible isometry group up to conjugation)
Links Ricci solitons with maximal symmetry, showing the soliton metric realizes maximal symmetry among invariant metrics
Develops the framework of AlgIsom and standard modifications to describe transitive solvable isometry groups
Identifies a canonical completely solvable subgroup that yields maximal symmetry (Theorem 3.2, Gordon–Wilson lineage)
Highlights structural relations via normal/standard modifications and completely solvable ideals

Representative Publications & Core Contr.Publication: Infinitesimal Maximal Symmetry and Ricci Soliton Solvmanifolds
Core Contributions: Introduces almost maximal and infinitesimal maximal symmetry notions for left-invariant metrics
Establishes an equivalence relation on simply-connected solvable Lie groups via modification theory, yielding a unique completely solvable representative per class
Proves that every left-invariant Ricci soliton on a simply-connected solvable Lie group is infinitesimally maximally symmetric
Shows uniqueness of left-invariant Ricci solitons up to scaling and isometry within a class (Corollaries 1.6, 1.8 in the paper’s framework)
Proves every left-invariant Einstein metric with negative Ricci curvature on a solvable Lie group is maximally symmetric
Provides a detailed mechanism via standard position, solvsolitons, and Einstein extensions to relate symmetry of the ambient Einstein metric to the solvable group
Gives explicit descriptions of Isom0(S,g) in the completely solvable unimodular case (Isom0(S,g) = S ⋊ Aut(S) ∩ O(g))
Connects to the Alekseevskii conjecture program and Ricci-flow stability considerations

Representative Publications & Core Contr.Publication: Einstein Solvmanifolds as Submanifolds of Symmetric Spaces
Core Contributions: Shows that simply-connected, completely solvable Einstein solvmanifolds embed isometrically and isomorphically into the lower-triangular matrix group T(n,R) endowed with a left-invariant symmetric metric
Provides constructive embedding results that extend Tamaru’s explicit examples to a general existence theorem
Introduces the admissible metric Lie algebra framework and explicit embedding steps (nilradical control, scaling alignment, abelian extension) to realize embeddings
Relates to Nash/Ado-type theorems in a homogeneous, left-invariant setting and clarifies limitations in the compact case

Representative Publications & Core Contr.Publication: Semi-Simple Lie Algebras Are Determined by Their Iwasawa Subalgebras
Core Contributions: Proves that non-compact real semisimple Lie algebras are completely determined by their Iwasawa subalgebras (s = a ⊕ n)
Shows that if Iwasawa subalgebras s1 and s2 are isomorphic, the ambient semisimple algebras g1 and g2 are isomorphic, and any isomorphism extends from s1 to g1
Outlines an explicit reconstruction procedure for g from data in its Iwasawa subalgebra, including recovering a Satake diagram from g≥0 = m ⊕ s and Der(s)–based identification of m
Discusses nilradical considerations, pre-Einstein derivations, and the role of split vs non-split forms in reconstruction
